## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (Q8_0-GGUF (TRANSCRIBE.CPP), needs ~2.5 GB, from [github.com/handy-computer](https://github.com/handy-computer/transcribe.cpp/blob/18947cf405f957195dd457db4e34c1cff9e88889/README.md))
   
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/handy-computer/transcribe.cpp.git && cd transcribe.cpp && cmake -B build && cmake --build build && hf download handy-computer/granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar-gguf granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar-Q8_0.gguf --local-dir models/granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar && build/bin/transcribe-cli -m models/granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar/granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar-Q8_0.gguf audio.wav
   ```

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/ibm-granite](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-speech-4.1-2b-nar)
